political_bio:
**Minister.** Parliamentary Secretary, Cabinet Office, 9 July 2024 to 6 September 2025, responsible for national resilience. On 7 July 2025 the Cabinet Office announced a national Emergency Alert test, naming her and Pat McFadden. The alert was sent to phones across the UK at 3pm on 7 September 2025. Her written statements were the Security and Intelligence Agencies Contingencies Fund advance (12 February 2025) and the Annual Report on Special Advisers 2025 (17 July 2025).

**Legislation.** Menstrual and Gynaecological Health Bill, a Ten Minute Rule bill, first reading on 18 March 2026. It had no second reading before the session ended on 29 April 2026 and has not been reintroduced.

**Family hubs.** Bexley Council runs a Family Hub at West Street, Erith, for families from pregnancy to age 18. Oppong-Asare campaigned for Sure Start style services and calls the Erith hub a campaign victory. Bexley Council's announcements do not attribute the hub to her. A second hub opened at Lakeside Medical Centre, Thamesmead, on 7 September 2026, with no role for her recorded.

**Pride in Place.** Up to £20 million over ten years (£2 million a year) for Thamesmead Birchmere Park, announced on 20 March 2026 by Oppong-Asare and the Leader of Greenwich Council. A neighbourhood board chair and vice chair were appointed in September 2026 to draw up a ten year plan. No project spending had been published by November 2026.

**DLR extension.** Her own website says she was first elected in 2019 on a pledge to campaign for it, and she launched the #NextStopThamesmead campaign that year. The Government backed it in the November 2025 Autumn Budget. TfL plans to apply for a Transport and Works Act Order in early 2027 and says construction could start by 2029, subject to funding and permissions, with opening possible in the early 2030s. Greenwich Council says it secured the commitment working alongside her.

**Superloop SL3.** TfL express bus between Thamesmead and Bromley North, now running. Greenwich Council lists it among work delivered alongside her.

**Thamesmead New Town.** Selected by the Government on 23 March 2026. Greenwich Council says the site is set to deliver up to 15,000 homes and 6,000 jobs; these are planned figures, not homes built or jobs created. Greenwich Council says it recommended the area together with her.

**Not attributed to her.** NHS England named Erith Health Centre for an upgrade on 26 March 2026. The Government awarded £23 million in December 2025 for a new SL11 bus scheme between Woolwich and Abbey Wood via Thamesmead. Neither announcement mentions her.
